chatHistory.content: I need an open-source alternative to Slack for a privacy-conscious team.

Here are solid open-source alternatives to **Slack** that you can **self-host** for a privacy-conscious team:

## Recommended (Slack-like team chat)

### 1) **Mattermost**
- Website: [Mattermost](https://mattermost.com)
- GitHub repo: [mattermost/mattermost](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost)
- Why it fits: Slack-style channels, team messaging, strong admin controls for hosting your own data.
- Maintenance: Actively maintained (recent commits + releases).

### 2) **Rocket.Chat**
- Website: [Rocket.Chat](https://rocket.chat/)
- GitHub repo: [RocketChat/Rocket.Chat](https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat)
- Why it fits: Channels, mentions, integrations, and a focus on self-hosted communication.
- Maintenance: Actively maintained (recent commits + releases).

### 3) **Zulip**
- Website: [Zulip](https://zulip.com)
- GitHub repo: [zulip/zulip](https://github.com/zulip/zulip)
- Why it fits: “Topic” threads (per-conversation organization) can feel very productive for teams compared to Slack’s linear threads/channels.
- Maintenance: Actively maintained (recent commits + releases).

## If you want federated chat / broader ecosystem
### 4) **Matrix Synapse** (homeserver)
- Documentation/website: [Element Synapse](https://element-hq.github.io/synapse)
- GitHub repo: [element-hq/synapse](https://github.com/element-hq/synapse)
- Why it fits: Federated messaging with strong privacy options when self-hosted; pairs well with Matrix clients.
- Maintenance: Actively maintained (recent commits + releases).

---

If you tell me:
1) whether you need **Slack-like threads** or prefer **topic-based** conversations, and  
2) whether you want **federation** (users across multiple servers) or **fully self-contained**,  
…I can narrow this to the best single choice.

User request:
For a franchise of dentist offices

For a **franchise of dentist offices**, here are strong open-source swaps for your selected tools (**Zapier** and **Zendesk**) that work well for managing **patient communication, follow-ups, and shared support workflows** across multiple locations.

## Zapier → workflow automation
### Recommended: [n8n](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n) (Website: https://n8n.io)
- Self-hostable workflow automation (Zapier-like “connect apps + automate tasks”)
- Good for automating things like: lead intake routing, appointment reminders, CRM updates, emailing staff when forms are submitted, etc.
- **Health:** actively maintained (latest release today)

### Also good: [Node-RED](http://nodered.org) (GitHub: https://github.com/node-red/node-red)
- Visual, event-driven automation builder
- Great if you want more “engineering control” or custom integrations
- **Health:** actively maintained (recent commits/releases)

### Also good: [Activepieces](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces) (Website: https://www.activepieces.com)
- No-code workflow automation with integrations
- **Health:** actively maintained (latest release today)

> Note: [Automatisch](https://github.com/automatisch/automatisch) is a Zapier alternative, but it is **not as recently updated** as the others.

## Zendesk → customer/patient support desk
### Recommended: [Chatwoot](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot) (Website: https://www.chatwoot.com/help-center)
- Shared inbox for multi-location support (email/chat), ticketing, tagging, and automation hooks
- Useful for handling patient questions, appointment requests, and escalation paths across franchises
- **Health:** actively maintained (latest commits/recent releases)

### Also strong: [Zammad](https://github.com/zammad/zammad) (Website: https://zammad.org)
- Helpdesk/ticketing for email + chat workflows
- **Health:** actively maintained (recent commits)

### Simpler/cheaper options
- [FreeScout](https://github.com/freescout-help-desk/freescout) (Website: https://freescout.net): shared inbox + ticketing
- [osTicket](https://github.com/osTicket/osTicket) (Website: https://osticket.com): classic ticketing
- **But:** these are generally less feature-rich than Chatwoot/Zammad for omnichannel/franchise-style workflows.

## Quick “dentist franchise” starter setup idea
- **Website form → n8n**: route inquiry to correct office/location + notify front desk
- **Patient inbox → Chatwoot**: shared “Appointments” inbox per location with tags like *New lead, Billing, Reschedule, Emergency*
- **Automation**: auto-create ticket, send confirmation email/SMS, set follow-up reminders, escalate overdue cases

If you tell me:
1) how many locations (and whether they share one brand inbox), and  
2) which channels you need (email only vs SMS vs live chat),  
…I can narrow this to the best 1–2 choices and suggest a concrete workflow map.

content.text:
For a **local library in Mississauga** (self-hosted / in-house use), here are solid “starter swap” alternatives to **Typeform** and **Notion** that you can run on your own server.

## 1) Typeform → Typeform alternative (surveys/forms)
- **Formbricks** — open-source Qualtrics/Typeform-style forms & surveys  
  Repo: [GitHub repo](https://github.com/formbricks/formbricks) • Website: [Formbricks](https://formbricks.com)  
  Health: actively maintained (last commit 1 day ago)

- **Typebot** — form + chatbot workflows (more “conversational” than classic forms)  
  Repo: [GitHub repo](https://github.com/baptisteArno/typebot.io) • Website: [Typebot](https://typebot.io)  
  Note: source-available license, not strictly OSI open-source  
  Health: actively maintained (last commit 3 days ago)

## 2) Notion → Notion alternative (docs/notes/wiki)
- **HedgeDoc** — team notes / wiki / Markdown documentation (very “library knowledge base” friendly)  
  Repo: [GitHub repo](https://github.com/hedgedoc/hedgedoc) • Website: [HedgeDoc](https://hedgedoc.org)  
  Health: actively maintained (last commit 5 days ago)

- **AFFiNE** — workspace for notes/docs/knowledge base (more feature-rich, still self-hostable)  
  Repo: [GitHub repo](https://github.com/toeverything/AFFiNE) • Website: [AFFiNE](https://affine.pro)  
  Health: actively maintained (last commit 2 days ago)

- **AppFlowy** — Notion-like wikis/projects/notes (self-hostable)  
  Repo: [GitHub repo](https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/AppFlowy) • Website: [AppFlowy](https://appflowy.com)  
  Note: maintenance is OK but commits are less frequent than the others.

## Suggested “library” setup
- Use **Formbricks** for: membership registration forms, program interest forms, event RSVP, feedback surveys.
- Use **HedgeDoc** for: internal policies, program guides, resource catalogs (as wiki pages), and staff notes.

If you tell me whether you want **OS-only open-source** (strict OSI licenses) or you’re OK with **source-available**, I’ll narrow this to the best 1–2 picks for each (and include a simple Mississauga library deployment plan).

content.text:
From the candidates we found, the **most permissive licenses** are:

## Most permissive (typically least restrictive)
- **Colanode** — **Apache 2.0** ([GitHub repo](https://github.com/colanode/colanode))  
  *Apache 2.0 is generally considered very permissive.*

- **AFFiNE** — **MIT** ([GitHub repo](https://github.com/toeverything/AFFiNE))  
  *MIT is also very permissive.*

## Next (still OSI, but more “copyleft” than MIT/Apache)
- **Formbricks** — **AGPL-3.0** (not in the “most permissive” group)
- **HedgeDoc** — **AGPL-3.0**
- **AppFlowy** — **AGPL-3.0**
- **Nextcloud Forms** — **AGPL-3.0**
- **HeyForm** — **AGPL-3.0**

## Not “most permissive”
- **Typebot** — **FSL-1.1** (source-available; not as permissive as MIT/Apache and not OSI-standard in the same way)
- **Form.io** — **OSL-3.0** (can be more restrictive than Apache/MIT)
- **OpnForm** — **license listed as “NOASSERTION”** in our dataset, so I wouldn’t treat it as permissive until you verify the actual license text.

### Quick answer
If you want the **most permissive**, pick:
- **MIT:** AFFiNE  
- **Apache 2.0:** Colanode  

If you want, tell me if you’re aiming for **notes/wiki** or **surveys/forms**, and I’ll suggest the best permissive option(s) for that specific use.
